operations.summary: read the words of a wisent-errors command line: the command it names, the operands it gives and the options it sets

causes.failed: reading the command wisent-errors was asked to run
causes.cause: the command line names no command, only options or nothing
causes.observed: the arguments were {quoted_arguments}; the commands are {commands}
causes.remedy: name one of the commands after the options, as in `wisent-errors --product <file> telemetry status`

causes.cause: wisent-errors has no command of that name
the command takes {wanted} and was given {given}
the command takes {wanted}, and {quoted_extra} is more than it reads
causes.remedy: drop {quoted_extra}, or quote an operand that holds spaces as one word, as in `{usage}`

causes.cause: {quoted_option} is not an option the command takes
causes.remedy: drop {quoted_option}, or write in its place an option the command takes, as in `{usage}`

causes.cause: the option takes a value and is the last word of the command line
causes.remedy: give its value right after it, as in `{option} {placeholder}`
give {what} as a whole number, as in `{usage}`

causes.failed: reading the code of the failure at {point}
causes.cause: {quoted_code} is not a code of the fleet's vocabulary
causes.remedy: name one of {codes}; catalogue/codes.json says what each one means

operations.summary: read the product file that names which product a telemetry, support or doctor command speaks for: its id, its app id and its version

causes.cause: the command speaks for a product and no --product names the product's file
causes.remedy: name the product's file before the command, as in `wisent-errors --product product.json {command}`: a JSON object with its id, app_id and version

operations.summary: hold a product's doctor findings to the functionalities its failure catalogue declares, and its warnings to the declaration rules, as the product's CI runs them

causes.remedy: name the file {source} printed, or print it again with {source}

causes.failed: holding the doctor's findings in {doctor} to the functionalities {listing} declares
causes.cause: {count} problem(s) keep the doctor from trying each functionality once: {problems}
causes.observed: {declared} functionality(ies) with an entry point declared, {findings} finding(s) reported
causes.remedy: give every functionality with an entry point one diagnosis check, a probe or a skip saying why, drop a second check and every check of a functionality the catalogue does not declare, then print the findings again with `<product> doctor --json`

causes.failed: holding the warnings {listing} declares to the declaration rules
causes.remedy: change each declaration as its problem says, in the product's code, then print the listing again with `<product> warnings list`
